children: Shares of aerospace and defense company Textron
jumped 11.3% in the morning session after the company reported higher third-quarter 2026 earnings and raised its full-year adjusted EPS and cash flow outlook.

According to a company press release, Textron reported that income from continuing operations reached $1.56 per share, up from $1.31 per share in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted income from continuing operations grew to $1.76 per share compared with $1.55 per share in the prior-year period. Textron also raised its full-year outlook for both adjusted EPS and cash flow. Raising annual projections alongside delivering year-over-year profit growth often reinforces market expectations for durable operational strength and healthy cash generation across Textron's business segments.
What is the market telling us

Textron’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. Moves this big are rare for Textron and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 7 months ago when the stock gained 4% on the news that the U.S. and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, pausing a conflict that had sent equity prices reeling.

The aerospace sector was projected to benefit from the broader "risk-on" move as commercial aviation prospects improved. While defense-related volatility remains a factor, the stabilization of global trade routes and the massive rally in airline stocks provided a halo effect for aircraft manufacturers and parts suppliers.

Textron is up 2.1% since the beginning of the year, but at $88.91 per share, it is still trading 11.8% below its 52-week high of $100.77 from February 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Textron’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,204.
